summary:
BioHab: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-playable educational simulation designed for students ages 7–12 to experience the real engineering and biological trade-offs of running a Lunar or Martian outpost over a 10-Sol mission.
Rather than oversimplifying space exploration, BioHab challenges young learners to balance three interconnected survival systems—Power, Bioregenerative Life Support (O2, water recycling, and food production), and Radiation Shielding—against real space hazards like lunar dust accumulation, deep shadows, and solar storms. Grounded in real NASA science from the Artemis program, ISS Veggie Plant Growth System, and ECLSS, every tactical choice shows transparent resource trade-offs (such as diverting recycled greywater into radiation-shielding walls or optimizing red/blue LED wavelengths for hydroponic crops) accompanied by bite-sized NASA science explanations and non-punitive failure diagnostics.
By combining systems engineering with closed-loop space biology in an accessible game format, BioHab turns complex mission constraints into intuitive, hands-on STEM discovery for the next generation of explorers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

BioHab: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based resource-management simulation built for the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge. Students command a lunar or Martian outpost across a 10-Sol mission, balancing three interconnected survival systems—Power (kW), Bioregenerative Life Support (O2, Water & Crops), and Radiation Shielding—against real space hazards like lunar dust buildup, deep shadows, and solar storms. Each Sol, players inspect interactive habitat modules (Solar Wing, Crew & Water Wall, Bio-Greenhouse, and ASTRO-BOT) and select two tactical engineering actions that preview exact resource trade-offs before execution.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Traditional STEM materials often oversimplify mission engineering or overwhelm young learners with raw equations. BioHab turns complex closed-loop life-support trade-offs into tangible cause-and-effect decisions. Built-in NASA science explanations and non-punitive mission debriefs—including a 10-Sol Telemetry History chart—help students understand why engineering compromises happen in real spaceflight.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Languages & Frameworks: React, TypeScript, HTML5, Tailwind CSS

- Visuals & Audio: Custom responsive inline SVGs and Web Audio API feedback

- Super Intelligence (SI) Acknowledgment: Built and debugged with the assistance of Google AI Studio (Gemini) for code generation, UI layout, and iterative troubleshooting.

- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and Google AI Studio (.ai.studio)

Creativity & Design Factors Considered:

To keep learners engaged without sacrificing scientific accuracy, we designed an interactive cross-section habitat where every subsystem reacts visually to player decisions, paired with an ASTRO-BOT mission companion and clear resource-delta badges (+Power, -Bio-Life, +Shield) grounded in NASA Artemis, ISS Veggie, and ECLSS research.

Hosting & Version Control: GitHub https://github.com/TanushreeSapare/biohab-mission-trainer and Google AI Studio (.ai.studio)
